mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last three weeks (-69.4 to -64.7), indicating a steady resumption of commuting and weekday errands that typically co-occur with retail and recreation trips, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -69.4 to -64.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its prior-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility (e.g., from -27.7 to +5.7) signals relaxation of outdoor-activity restrictions; once such a threshold crossing occurs, retail and recreation venues typically reopen or see eased capacity limits within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 20 points week-on-week, crossing from negative to positive
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after a PARKS jump exceeding 20 points, or PARKS subsequently falls back without RETAIL_REC response, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve simultaneously (as seen over the last three weeks), it indicates a joint behavioral shift toward normal out-of-home routines (commuting plus transit use), which compounds to drive stronger recovery in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -76.4 to -73.0 and WORKPLACES rose from -69.4 to -64.7 concurrently
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed its backward mean despite concurrent improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily each week (29.3 to 26.7), suggesting a seasonal/behavioral shift away from home-bound routines as weather warms; in a reopening regime this steady decline is expected to continue feeding increased retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 29.3 to 26.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not rise relative to its prior mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rebounded sharply from -35.0 to -29.3 over the last two weeks, a leading indicator that consumers are resuming routine errands; once this rebound exceeds a 5-point threshold over two weeks, broader retail and recreation trips typically follow within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by more than 5 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -35.0 (t-2w) to -29.3 (t-1w and t-0w)
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM's rebound exceeds 5 points but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not increase relative to the current week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Despite recent improvement, TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (-73.0), indicating that public transit restrictions or fear of transit use persist; in a still-tightening or early-easing regime, this persistent transit suppression caps the recovery of retail and recreation mobility, keeping RETAIL_REC flat or lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has stayed between -76.4 and -73.0 across all four weeks
regime_hint: early easing with transit still restricted
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean rises above its backward mean while TRANSIT remains below -70, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse co-movement of RESIDENTIAL (declining) and RETAIL_REC (rising) over the last three weeks reflects a direct behavioral substitution: as households spend less time at home, they redirect that time toward retail and recreation activity, a pattern expected to persist.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 28.7 to 26.7 while RETAIL_REC rose from -80.1 to -77.1 over the same period
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline over the next week but RETAIL_REC does not rise in tandem, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in PARKS (volatile but net positive) and WORKPLACES mobility signals combined outdoor recreation demand and commuting resumption; when both rise together over two weeks, the compounded effect accelerates retail and recreation recovery beyond what either alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS net improved from -7.0 to -3.6 and WORKPLACES improved from -69.4 to -64.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS and WORKPLACES both rise over two weeks but RETAIL_REC's forward 2-week mean does not exceed its backward mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
